items.title: Goyal calls for trusted India-US supply chains
items.summary: New Delhi: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal on Thursday called for building resilient and trusted supply chains between India and the US amid prevailing global uncertainties.This helps countries reduce dependence on one geography, securing supplies of critical goods and strengthening India-US economic and strategic ties, the minister said.Addressing the Indo-US Economic Summit here, he said huge potential exists between the two countries to enhance economic cooperation, as the US offers capital, technology, and innovation, while India offers skills, talent, manufacturing strength, and competitiveness.Goyal said he would conclude with five calls to action, using the acronym TRUST to outline his suggestions."T - the first letter. Let us turn our supply chains into resilient and trusted supply chains. 'R', let us raise our talent together with our friendly and partner countries," he said.The minister suggested increasing collaborations between Indian and US universities."I am working with some of them to bring them to India. We'd like to invite all US universities and students to look at India as a part of their program. Because I firmly believe global growth is going to be led from countries in Asia, Africa and Latin America. And time spent by students from the developed world in Indian universities and Indian colleges will help them learn how to deal with us," he added.He said 'S' in the TRUST acronym stands for 'Speak', urging both sides to communicate candidly and openly flag any hurdles or difficulties they face."Let us Speak to each other candidly. Let us flag off the hurdles or the difficulties that anybody faces. So that we can work as your partners to help you in your work. We have different arms of the government which will support you in your work. And help you take your work, take your business to the world," Goyal said.He said the final 'T' stood for 'Track', emphasising the need to monitor outcomes, ensure accountability for performance and urging the IACC to hold both sides accountable.He added that India and the US are two vibrant democracies which shape the global narrative and are important engines for global growth."...an engine always runs on fuel, and that fuel, when it comes to India, is trust. India offers a trusted partnership. India offers our trust, a partner who will stand by you through thick and thin. In every crisis, India is that one partner which never lets its friends down," he added.In a volatile and uncertain world, countries face challenges due to the ongoing wars and the West Asia crisis."In these uncertain times, the world no longer needs just supply chains. They need trusted supply chains. In a trust chain, the partner shares your vision, respects the rule of law, honours contracts and therefore India and the US are natural links who build a chain of trust, a trusted chain. These strong bonds are reflected in our engagement at every level," the minister noted.The minister said the country's exports of goods and services have reached an all-time high of USD 90 billion."That is the India growth story. And that is the story we wish to share with our friends like the United States of America," he added.Meanwhile, speaking at the FICCI event, Goyal said that the country would achieve the USD one trillion exports target during the current fiscal.He added that India must move beyond reducing its dependence on the world and instead make the world dependent on India.He urged FICCI to remake itself as a global chamber at its centenary celebrations.The country, Goyal said, now has the capital, talent, entrepreneurs and banking strength to raise its ambition."Last time I came to your AGM, I spoke about reducing dependence on the world and becoming self-reliant. Today I would like to suggest going one step forward," he said, adding, "We need to make the world dependent upon us. We need to create leverage in India".On trade pacts, he said before 2014, India's free trade agreements covered partners representing USD 10 trillion of global GDP, and the agreements concluded in the past four and a half years have added USD 60 trillion.Negotiations with eight or nine further geographies over the next 18 months would add another USD 15 trillion, giving Indian exporters preferential access to USD 85 trillion, or 76 per cent of global GDP, he added.

items.title: Putin rules out truce after Crimea bridge strike
items.summary: MOSCOW: Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Thursday that Moscow would no longer consider a moratorium on strikes in the Black Sea or on energy infrastructure following Ukraine's attacks on the bridge linking Russia and Crimea, vowing a harsh response.Earlier, Kyiv struck the bridge for the third time in a week, creating an awkward backdrop to three-way talks Putin held with the Chinese and US presidents at an APEC summit in Shenzhen.Speaking after those talks, Putin said he had discussed a possible halt to attacks at sea and on energy facilities with Russia's Security Council and had "asked everyone to give it further thought and come back to it, hoping that perhaps some kind of agreement could be reached.""But after the strikes on the Crimean Bridge, there will be no agreements. We will respond to these strikes. And I want everyone to know this: I believe our response will be far more painful than what the Kyiv regime did to the bridge," he said.He added that the bridge was used exclusively for civilian purposes and not to transport military equipment, as Kyiv has alleged, or petroleum products."We will, of course, restore the bridge. The road section suffered serious damage," he said.

items.title: Airtel takes top spot, HDFC loses brand crown
items.summary: Mumbai: India’s top 100 brands lost 12% of their combined value in the past year, as declines in technology and financial services outweighed gains in automobiles and retail. Airtel displaced HDFC Bank to become the country’s most valuable brand for the first time, according to Kantar’s 2026 BrandZ ranking.The combined value of the top 100 stood at $460.3 billion, equivalent to 11% of India’s GDP. Airtel’s brand value rose 5% to $43.2 billion, while HDFC Bank ranked second at $35.6 billion, followed by Tata Consultancy Services at $24.1 billion.The decline was driven disproportionately by business-to-business and consumer technology brands, as well as some large financial services companies, said Soumya Mohanty, managing director, South Asia at Kantar.Read more: Indian brands hit $523.5 billion valuation as HDFC Bank leads Kantar BrandZ 2025 Ranking“Growth is not guaranteed anymore. The rising tide, which was raising all boats earlier, is no longer happening. We will see strong brands being pulled apart from weaker brands,” Mohanty said.Kantar found that Indian brands which strengthened their Meaningful Difference, a measure of distinctiveness and relevance to consumers, grew by an average of 7%, while those with flat or declining scores lost 13%.The decline contrasts with a 22% rise in global brand value, driven largely by artificial intelligence companies and technology platforms. India has less exposure to these categories, Kantar said.Read more: Adani CFO pushes back on Uday Kotak's comparison of Anthropic with India's top companiesDeepender Rana, Kantar’s executive managing director for South Asia, said India’s expanding economy offered opportunities for mass-market and premium brands, but inflation was weighing on consumer decisions.“Brands need to chart a course that confidently balances short-term pressures with long-term brand building,” Rana said.Airtel’s brand value has risen 210% since 2020, supported by its expansion beyond connectivity into digital services. It is the first telecom operator to top the ranking since its launch in 2014.Meesho was the biggest riser, with brand value climbing 64% to $1.9 billion, followed by Royal Enfield, up 60% to $3.8 billion. Financial services remained the largest category, accounting for 29% of the top 100’s value.Blinkit was the highest-ranked new entrant at No. 27, with a brand value of $4.3 billion. India had three brands in the global top 100: Airtel, HDFC Bank and TCS. Jio was excluded because its valuation was conducted before its stock market listing.

items.title: Nations gear up for esports showdown
items.summary: The Esports Foundation (EF) has expanded the qualification and competition framework for the inaugural Esports Nations Cup (ENC) in November 2027, introducing regional online tournaments, National Team Partner-led events, larger national rosters and a year-round ranking system.The expanded Road to ENC 2027 is aimed at giving players more opportunities to represent their countries and territories, while building national rivalries and fan engagement in the run-up to the tournament's Finals.The first ENC qualification season saw nearly 200,000 players compete across 210 regional qualifiers. Around 2,000 players representing 123 countries and territories secured places at the competition. All places earned by national teams in 2026 will be protected, with the players who qualified included in the expanded national rosters from which coaches will select their Finals squads.Countries and territories that did not qualify in 2026 will get another opportunity through a fresh set of regional online tournaments, followed by a final LAN qualifier.The regional online qualifiers will begin on February 26, 2027, and run for five weeks across multiple game titles. Seven regional winners and one invited nation from the ENC Solidarity programme will advance to the final LAN qualifier to compete for the remaining places. Game-specific schedules and details of the LAN event will be announced later.“Representing your nation is one of the proudest moments in any athlete’s career. For fans, supporting their country or territory can be their first connection to a sport and the beginning of a lasting passion,” said Ralf Reichert, CEO of the Esports Foundation.“As we build towards the first Esports Nations Cup, we want to help national teams grow together and give fans a team to believe in. Road to ENC creates more opportunities for those teams to compete and for fans to get to know the players, follow emerging rivalries, and become a part of their team’s journey. When those teams arrive at ENC 2027, we want fans to have been part of how they got there.”**Four pillars of the expanded qualification framework**The expanded Road to ENC will operate through four key elements, starting with events organised by National Team Partners (NTPs). These partners will be able to host local activations, friendly matches and multi-nation invitationals, giving national teams more opportunities to compete and coaches a chance to assess emerging players.The events will receive support through the ENC Development Fund, with the objective of building national fan bases and strengthening local esports ecosystems. NTPs can submit proposals for events scheduled in 2027 until the end of December 2026.The second element is the new qualification pathway for countries and territories that missed out on the 2026 qualification season. The regional online tournaments and subsequent LAN qualifier will offer another route into the Finals, with seven regional winners and one nation invited through the ENC Solidarity programme competing for the remaining spots.The third is an expansion of national team rosters. Coaches will be allowed to add eligible players to squads that qualified in 2026, giving them greater flexibility to test combinations in national team matches before finalising their line-ups. Updated expanded rosters must be submitted by January 15, 2027, while Finals squads must be selected by May 31, 2027.For individual or solo game titles, however, the qualifying spot will remain with the player who earned it for their country or territory.The fourth element is the ENC Ranking, which will track the performance of national teams throughout the year. Players will earn points for their countries and territories through results in international club leagues and tournaments, as well as national team competitions.The rankings will evolve as the season progresses, providing fans with an ongoing view of their national team's standing. They will also be used to determine seeding for the ENC group-stage draw and inform direct invitations to future editions of the competition.The Esports Foundation said more details on the ranking system, qualification schedules and National Team Partner-led events would be announced in the coming weeks.The Esports Nations Cup is a global competition bringing together players from different countries and territories across multiple esports titles. Its inaugural Finals are scheduled for November 2027.

items.summary: The US Federal Reserve is monitoring financial stability risks stemming from aggressive investment in artificial intelligence (AI) and elevated asset valuations, as policymakers warned that disappointing returns from the technology boom could trigger broader financial market disruptions, Reuters reported.Minutes of the Fed's October 27-28 policy meeting, released on Wednesday, showed that officials were concerned about the potential consequences of heavy AI-related borrowing, rising leverage among hedge funds and concentrated exposure to a small number of companies.According to Reuters, Fed policymakers and central bank staff raised these concerns as part of a broader assessment of vulnerabilities in the financial system. The review found that elevated asset valuations and hedge fund leverage were among the most significant sources of risk, although strong balance sheets among banks and households offered some protection against severe financial shocks.Read more: South Korean shares fall over 1% as hawkish Fed remarks weigh on sentimentPolicymakers were particularly concerned about the possibility that returns on AI investments could fall short of investor expectations. The minutes highlighted the rapid growth of AI-related debt, much of which has been channelled through complex and relatively opaque financing structures, Reuters reported.Some officials also flagged the concentration of AI exposure among a limited number of companies, raising concerns that setbacks involving major players could have wider consequences for financial markets and the economy.Hedge funds emerged as another area of concern, with policymakers identifying high leverage and limited capacity among financial dealers to intermediate transactions as potential channels through which market stress could intensify, Reuters reported,Although Fed staff described the financial system as resilient and noted that banks had ample access to liquidity, some policymakers cautioned that vulnerabilities within the banking sector could emerge rapidly despite initially reassuring assessments. Officials also questioned whether existing regulatory data fully captured the extent of financial institutions' exposure to potential risks.Read more: Japan stocks fall as metal shares slide; investors await Anthropic IPO debutFed weighs measures to strengthen financial resilienceThe minutes also revealed discussions among policymakers about measures to improve the financial system's ability to withstand future disruptions.A few officials considered increasing capital requirements for banks, while others emphasised the importance of ensuring that lenders were better prepared to access the Fed's emergency lending discount window during periods of market stress.Some policymakers also discussed the possibility of creating a dedicated asset-purchasing mechanism aimed specifically at addressing financial stability risks.The debate comes as the Federal Reserve reassesses how it uses its balance sheet as a policy tool. Its holdings expanded significantly following large-scale bond-buying programmes introduced during the 2008 global financial crisis and the COVID-19 pandemic.According to Reuters, the pandemic-era bond purchases initially designed to stabilise markets eventually evolved into a broader monetary stimulus programme, highlighting the challenges of distinguishing between emergency market support and conventional monetary easing.Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack has advocated a more clearly defined framework for such interventions, including an exit strategy to unwind bond holdings once financial stability has been restored. She has argued that any asset-purchasing programme should be temporary, with holdings sold in a timely manner after market conditions normalise, Reuters reported.Several policymakers, however, cautioned against relying on monetary policy to address financial market disruptions, suggesting that other tools may be more appropriate for containing emerging vulnerabilities.The minutes also showed that almost all Fed policymakers believed further interest rate increases could be necessary if the economy developed in line with their expectations. Officials had kept interest rates unchanged at the October meeting amid persistent inflation concerns.The growing importance of AI and technology investment in driving economic growth could complicate the Fed's policy decisions if a significant correction in the sector were to threaten broader financial stability.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

India's next export story after pharma and IT
items.summary: New Delhi: India has the potential to replicate its success in the pharmaceutical and information technology sectors across emerging industries such as electronics, which could emerge as major export drivers while also supporting import substitution, said Naina Lal Kidwai, Economist, former banker and Founder and Chair of Rothschild India.Speaking to on the sidelines of the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry's (FICCI) Annual General Meeting and Annual Convention, Kidwai expressed confidence that India's export growth momentum could continue, citing the country's achievements in pharmaceuticals, information technology, electronics and automobile manufacturing."I see no reason why not, because we've seen the success in the electronics sector. India, in any case, is the pharmacy to the world, and we've seen success in the IT sector. We have shown that in the sectors we choose to embrace, we can succeed, and it is now for us to widen that success," she said.Highlighting the potential of emerging industries, Kidwai said India was witnessing similar progress in automobiles and auto ancillaries, while defence and electronics could emerge as significant contributors to the country's exports."We are looking at new sectors like defence and electronics, which at one level are import substitutes, but at another level can be huge export drivers as well," she added.Referring to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's address to the industry, Kidwai stressed the need for Indian manufacturers to focus on producing quality goods for international markets while strengthening domestic industrial capabilities.She emphasised that India should look beyond its domestic market and tap global opportunities by encouraging investment in manufacturing and building a resilient industrial ecosystem."We have to make quality goods not just for India but for export. Let's embrace global markets. Let's invest in India for global markets and let's look at import substitution so that we have a resilient domestically dependent industry," she said.She also highlighted India's dependence on imported active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), intermediate products and steel, referring to the Prime Minister's emphasis on strengthening domestic manufacturing.On the energy front, Kidwai said the government had cushioned the impact of the fossil fuel crisis by maintaining imports from Russia and providing a buffer against fluctuations in domestic fuel prices.She noted that elevated crude oil prices were contributing to inflationary pressures, while improved movement of shipments through the Strait of Hormuz could help India restore its import flows.Highlighting the significance of easing global crude prices for the Indian economy, she said a decline in international oil prices would benefit the country."Clearly, the price of Brent and crude coming down is going to be a winner for us," she said.

items.title: Centre proposes separate licensing norms for wholesale trade of bulk drugs
items.summary:
The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed a separate licensing framework for the wholesale trade of bulk drugs, including active and inactive bulk substances, to strengthen regulatory oversight and accountability in the pharmaceutical supply chain.
The proposed amendments to the Drugs Rules, 1945, seek to introduce separate application (19-BC) and licence (20-BC) forms for the wholesale of bulk drugs, distinct from the existing licensing provisions for formulations.
At present, a common licence covers the wholesale of both formulations and bulk drugs.
The proposed amendment seeks to establish a dedicated licensing framework for bulk drugs, enabling more focused regulatory oversight of their wholesale trade and greater accountability in the pharmaceutical supply chain, the ministry said in a statement.

items.title: Trump, Putin hold bilateral talks in China on sidelines of Apec Summit
items.summary:
US President Donald Trump and his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin on Thursday held bilateral talks ahead of three-way talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping.
The meeting marked the first time Trump and Putin have held talks since their discussions in Alaska last year that failed to broker a deal to ease Russia's war in Ukraine.
"Wonderful things can come out of this - or at least start," Trump said after joining Putin for the one-on-one meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Summit, calling Putin "my friend."
"We've had a great relationship for many years," Trump said after shaking hands with Putin. Their meeting together lasted roughly 40 minutes.
Trump has frequently boasted of his rapport with Putin, even as relations between the US and Ukraine appear to have cratered recently.
Trump rejected new Russia sanctions, while Kyiv was undermined by disruptions in satellite support for its drones during the war.

items.title: Maruti Suzuki, Tata Motors PV, other auto stocks soar up to 7%; Nifty Auto index jumps 4%. What’s driving the rally?
items.summary: Shares of automobile companies, including Tata Motors, Maruti Suzuki and M&M, rallied up to 7% on Thursday, lifting the Nifty Auto index by 4%. The gains came as aluminium, copper and other key metals used in the industry fell to a seven-month low, easing concerns over rising input costs.Maruti Suzuki, India’s largest carmaker, was the biggest gainer in the pack, surging over 6.5% to Rs 13,487 apiece on the BSE, while Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles gained 4%. M&M advanced 5% to Rs 3,508 per share. Hyundai Motor India shares also rose over 4% to Rs 2,193 apiece, while commercial vehicle maker Ashok Leyland climbed over 2%.Metal prices tumbleOn Wednesday, benchmark three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange (LME) fell for a fifth consecutive session, touching its lowest level since April 13, Reuters reported. Prices recovered marginally on Thursday.Also read: Japan stocks fall as metal shares slide; investors await Anthropic IPO debut"The current move in LME copper prices looks more like relief than a decisive turn. The sharp retreat was driven by a buoyant US dollar and growing question marks over the pace of the AI data-center buildout, where copper is a key input in the infrastructure, Reuters cited Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade."The main factors to watch remain the path of the dollar, any further signals on AI-related capital spending, and Chinese demand indicators." Further, aluminum hit a 51-month low, while tin prices plunged to an 8-month low.Domestic brokerage Emkay says the sell-off is primarily driven by a stronger US dollar and weakness in global equity markets, triggering widespread profit booking and long liquidation. Traders also appeared to reduce positions to manage mark-to-market (M2M) losses.Notably, Wednesday recorded the highest single-day trading volume compared with the average daily volumes of the previous month, indicating significant position unwinding and heightened market activity.Meanwhile, China's uneven economic recovery and concerns over demand from its construction and manufacturing sectors are weighing on sentiment, experts say.Higher crude oil prices have also influenced the outlook for industrial metals. Rising energy costs increase expenses across the mining, smelting, refining, and transportation chain. Aluminium and zinc, in particular, are highly sensitive to power costs.While higher costs can sometimes support commodity prices by constraining supply, markets are currently more focused on the risks to economic growth. Rising energy costs can curb business activity, industrial production and consumer spending, ultimately weakening demand for metals used in construction, machinery, infrastructure and automobiles.Read more: Base metals lose momentum amid strong dollar and demand concernsWhy could auto companies benefit?The decline in copper, aluminium and tin prices could provide relief to Indian automakers by lowering raw-material costs. These metals are used in vehicle manufacturing, electrical components, wiring, engines and other auto parts. Cheaper inputs can reduce production expenses and ease pressure on operating margins. Aluminium, copper, rubber, and plastic components account for 40-45% of passenger vehicle raw material costs.Foreign brokerage Jefferies said the earnings outlook for auto OEMs weakened in CY26 primarily due to the intense commodity cost rally. It added that the auto industry faces a high base of volumes starting 2HFY27 as commodity cost pressures continue, albeit at a lower intensity than seen in the first half of the financial year.Disclaimer: This article has been written by Veer Sharma, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. items.title: Red metal feels the blues! Voltas, Blue Star, other AC stocks jump up to 6% as copper prices hit 7-month lows
items.summary: Shares of AC majors, including Voltas, Blue Star and PG Electroplast, jumped up to 6% on Thursday as copper prices hit the weakest level in seven months after recording the biggest single-day plunge since US President Donald Trump unveiled global tariffs in April 2025.Voltas shares jumped more than 5% to Rs 1,192.90 apiece on NSE, while Blue Star shares surged over 5% to Rs 1,709.10 apiece on Thursday morning. PG Electroplast, which makes components for air conditioners, saw its shares jump around 6% to trade near Rs 571 apiece.Also read | India’s $25 bn copper drive moves from building smelters to securing minesThe benchmark copper contracts on the London Metal Exchange dropped to their lowest level since April 7 on Wednesday. This came on the back of a stronger dollar, growing concerns over Chinese industrial demand, and the sharp selloff in AI-linked stocks that have overshadowed the tightening of copper supplies.Why are copper prices falling?The US dollar hovered near a 19-month high on Thursday after Federal Reserve meeting minutes and hawkish comments from a Federal Reserve official hinted towards further interest rate hikes in the near term. Minutes from the FOMC meeting showed that officials of the American central bank saw a growing risk last month that they needed to intensify their efforts to control inflation, even as they kept rates steady. Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh on Monday said that emerging technologies will have a significant impact on the economy, but the possible scenarios range from rising growth with broadly shared gains to higher unemployment and a potential slowdown if anticipated investment returns prove disappointing. Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid on Sunday said that inflation was still "running too hot" and that the American central bank had "some work to do" to bring price pressures under control. Market traders are now seeing a nearly 90% chance of a 25-basis-point rate hike by the US Federal Reserve following its FOMC meeting in December, while the probability of a larger 50-basis-point move is priced at 10%, according to CME's FedWatch tool.The FOMC minutes will be closely watched, as they may provide further insights into the Federal Reserve's monetary policy outlook, which could have a broader impact on the commodities basket, said Axis Securities.Meanwhile, the sharp drop in copper prices also comes amid rising worries over the health of China’s economy, with analysts pointing out that a prolonged property downturn in the country could weigh on copper prices due to the metal’s extensive use in construction, electrical wiring and infrastructure. Additionally, the sharp selloff in the AI-linked stocks also bears an impact on copper prices as the frenzy over the nascent technology fizzles out, raising worries over the spending boom behind new data centres. Copper is essential for electrical infrastructure, making it sensitive to investments linked to artificial intelligence.Also read | Is AI selloff a window to buy? Morgan Stanley sees multiple buying opportunities on Wall StreetHow have AC stocks been performing recently?The consistent drop in copper prices has been boosting AC stocks recently, as the metal is one of the key components of the appliance. Voltas shares have gained 7% in a week and 17% in a month. Blue Star shares have jumped 8% in a week and 9% in a month.PG Electroplast shares have recorded marginal losses over a week but jumped 12% in a month. Pew said if current trends continue, there will be more than 3.6 billion Muslims and just under three billion Christians worldwide by 2070.
The absolute number of Hindus in India and worldwide will rise from 1.2 billion in 2020 to 1.4 billion by 2070.
But the rest of the world's population -- i.e., all non-Hindus -- will grow at an even faster rate. As a result, Hindus will shrink slightly as a share of the global population, falling from 15 per cent in 2020 to 14 per cent in 2070.
The world's total population is projected to increase by 29 per cent between 2020 and 2070, with Christians growing by 30 per cent and Muslims by 80 per cent.

items.title: India's IPO market set for bumper December as 6 firms prepare listings
items.summary: Mumbai: An eclectic mix of niche consumer businesses-from luxury catering and commercial gym equipment makers to baby- and adult-hygiene products and B2B hospitality providers-would seek to collectively raise about ₹10,000-12,000 crore through initial public offerings (IPOs) in December, rounding off a likely record year of share sales for India's primary markets.Foodlink F&B Holdings (luxury catering and banqueting), Jerai Fitness (commercial gym equipment), Swara Baby Products (disposable hygiene products), Nobel Hygiene (baby- and adult-hygiene products), Cult.fit (fitness and wellness) and PRISM, formerly OYO (global hospitality technology), are among the companies preparing for their market debut, bankers told ET.135974641Several of these companies operate in niche segments, with very few or no directly comparable listed players in India. "Investors now look for exposure to consumption themes that were earlier accessible only through private markets: premium experiences, fitness and wellness, and everyday hygiene," said Neha Agarwal, managing director and head of equity capital markets, JM Financial. The companies cited above have already received regulatory approvals for share sales and plan to launch their issues next month.Read more: Explained: Why did central banks just buy 320 tonnes of gold this quarter and can this last amid uncertainty?Rising disposable incomes, urbanisation and growing health awareness are creating large, under-penetrated categories, and these companies have built scale and brand recall in these segments.For promoters and private equity backers, deep domestic liquidity as well as strong participation from mutual funds and retail investors make this a good window to list, Agarwal said.Also, with financialisation, more varied companies are approaching the market, but each company is a clear market leader in its niche, whether from the standpoint of geography or business category, said Arka Mookerjee, partner at JSA.Read more: Largecaps pull ahead of small and mid caps in Q2 profit growth by over 25%. What’s driving the gap?"The regulatory landscape is also changing rapidly to track the feedback from each new issuance. A new ICDR (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) regulation is on the horizon and hopefully that will help get more of the next-100 companies on to the main boards," he said.Calendar year 2026, which saw the mega IPOs of Jio Platforms and the National Stock Exchange (NSE), is on course to end in a bumper haul for India's primary markets, which garnered Rs 1.58 lakh crore in IPOs until October despite a rather listless secondary market. The Sensex and the Nifty, which had underperformed until then, have since climbed more than 10% each on robust foreign fund flows.Among the companies preparing to list, Foodlink F&B Holdings has planned an IPO with a fresh issue of Rs 160 crore and offer for sale (OFS) of 12 million shares. The company is promoted by Sanjay Vazirani and operates across luxury catering, banqueting, casual dining restaurants and cloud kitchens.It has operations in India, the UAE, the UK and Malaysia.The proposed IPO by Jerai Fitness will entirely be an OFS of 4.39 million shares. The company manufactures strength and cardiovascular equipment for gyms, hotels, clubs, residential and commercial projects, and educational institutions.Its products are sold under the Jerai Fitness and Reebok brands.The IPO of Swara Baby Products, likely of Rs 1,000 crore, consists of a fresh issue and an OFS. The company manufactures disposable hygiene products across baby care, adult incontinence and feminine hygiene categories.The Nobel Hygiene IPO will comprise a fresh issue of Rs 150 crore and OFS of 15.5 million shares. It has built a presence across adult, baby and feminine absorbent hygiene categories.Its Friends brand pioneered the adult absorbent hygiene category in India.Cult.fit has planned an IPO of Rs 4,000 crore, consisting of a fresh issue and an OFS. The company is the only fitness and active lifestyle platform in India with a presence across both fitness services and fitness products.PRISM (OYO) has planned an IPO of Rs 3,350 crore. It has a distinctive B2B and B2C hospitality technology model, providing hotels with inventory visibility and dynamic pricing capabilities across online travel platforms.According to valuation experts, the absence of listed peers could make valuation a key challenge for these companies.These are categories built on rising discretionary spending, ageing demographics and changing urban lifestyles; public investors have not really had a way to own them until now, according to Dev Chandrasekhar, partner at Mumbai-based valuations and strategic advisory firm Transcendum."The catch is that when a company has no listed peer, there is nothing to anchor its price. The ones relying on 'first-of-its-kind' scarcity to command a premium may find that premium fading after listing, once the novelty wears off and quarterly numbers begin to arrive," said Chandrasekhar.Agarwal from JM Financial said that the scarcity of comparable listed peers can work in their favour, since investors are willing to pay for differentiated businesses. Valuation discipline remains essential, though. Companies that show clear unit economics and a credible path to profitability will see the strongest response, she said.

items.title: Tata Sons may shift listing onus to board, chair
items.summary: Mumbai: Tata Sons is understood to be preparing for a board meeting on November 26, armed with a detailed statement on its listing plans vetted by senior advocate Harish Salve that puts the onus on the board and chairman to comply with the Reserve Bank of India's instruction. The meeting is expected to bring into sharper focus the differences between Tata Sons and its principal shareholder, Tata Trusts, over whether the group holding company should remain privately held or comply with RBI's regulatory requirement to list it.The central bank sent a letter to Tata Sons on November 16 that it must comply with all applicable regulations governing upper layer non-banking financial companies, "including the requirement of listing by your company." This was in response to Tata Sons' October 6 communication seeking RBI's guidance on compliance with the regulations.Also Read: Tata Sons board to review Air India turnaround progressMonetisation of SP Group StakeTata group's holding company is likely to detail the listing strategy and how it proposes to take this forward at the November 26 meeting, said executives aware of the matter.135970562Tata Sons may also turn down an alternative restructuring proposal backed by Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata, arguing that RBI's rejection of the application to surrender its registration as a core investment company has left it with little scope to avoid a stock market listing. The legal presentation is expected to emphasise that the board and its chairman have a responsibility to initiate the compliance process, rather than pursue alternatives that could delay it, people familiar with the developments said.Also Read: Darius Khambata hits back at Venu Srinivasan, Vijay SinghTata Sons did not comment.Chairman N Chandrasekaran is likely to hold a private meeting with Shapoor Mistry ahead of the board meeting, to directly discuss the monetisation of Shapoorji Pallonji Group's 18.4% stake in Tata Sons and the group's funding requirements.Tata Sons' position is that monetisation of the Mistry-led SP Group's stake is not a matter for Noel Tata to address in his capacity as Tata Trusts chairman, according to people familiar with the company's thinking.SP Group, which is urgently seeking funds to repay borrowings, wants Tata Sons to buy back about ₹25,000 crore worth of its shares over the next 24 months. Noel Tata tabled this request from SP Group to the Tata Sons board at the last meeting on September 17."There cannot be any delay in the matter of listing. It is now a regulatory matter and the directive from RBI is clear. The restructuring proposal will be disposed of by Tata Sons. Tata Trusts had sent the restructuring proposal directly to RBI in September and Tata Sons will not consider the matter at all," said an executive.The holding company may also seek to finalise a date for its much-delayed AGM.Tata Trusts, which owns about 66% of Tata Sons, has been pushing for an alternative restructuring plan that could help the holding company avoid a listing. Noel Tata is expected to argue that the board should challenge RBI's September decision and reconsider the proposal submitted to the central bank.The proposal envisages merging Tata Electronics Systems Solutions and Tata Consulting Engineers with Tata Sons, giving the holding company an operating income stream and potentially changing its regulatory profile. The restructuring requires corporate, shareholder and regulatory approvals.Tata Sons has been classified as an upper-layer NBFC due to its large asset size and status as a core investment company. Under RBI's scale-based regulatory framework, upper-layer NBFCs are required to list their equity shares on a recognised stock exchange within three years of being identified in that category.Ashish K Singh, managing partner at Capstone Legal, said Tata Sons' only option to challenge RBI's order was to file a writ petition before the Bombay High Court, with the company itself being the appropriate party to initiate proceedings as the entity directly affected by the directive. "The decision, however, would have to be taken by the Tata Sons board collectively, and no such decision has been taken so far," Singh said. "The absence of a quorum at Tata Trusts was also an additional factor, limiting its influence over decision-making at Tata Sons," he said.Tata Trusts has a meeting scheduled for November 20 to revisit its opposition to the listing and discuss restructuring alternative. Neville Tata and Bhaskar Bhat are expected to support Noel Tata's position against listing and favour exploring the restructuring route, the people cited earlier said.

items.title: Smallcap earnings boom strengthens investment case despite valuation concerns
items.summary: Mumbai: Investors betting on India's mid-cap and small-cap stocks may have reasons to stay put even as concerns over valuations simmer and the recent shift in market momentum towards large caps. The September quarter earnings performance of smaller companies continues to keep the case for investing in these segments strong, with smallcaps posting their strongest profit growth in seven quarters. Analysts, however, caution that margin pressures and elevated valuations warrant a selective approach.The combined net profit of 208 companies in the BSE 250 SmallCap Index, excluding BFSI (banking, finance, insurance) and oil and gas firms, surged 38% year-on-year in the September quarter, the strongest growth in seven quarters. Operating profit rose 28.6%, its fastest pace in 12 quarters, while revenue increased 24.18%, the highest growth in 17 quarters.135974300Midcap companies also reported healthy earnings growth, though the pace of profit expansion slowed. The combined net profit of 109 companies in the BSE 150 Mid Cap Index, excluding BFSI and oil and gas firms, increased 17.86% year-on-year, compared with 21.65% in the previous quarter. Revenue grew 21%, its strongest increase in 17 quarters.Shankar Sharma, founder of GQuant and First Global, said the earnings performance reinforced his bullish view on smaller companies.Read more: Explained: Why did central banks just buy 320 tonnes of gold this quarter and can this last amid uncertainty?"The smaller companies have been doing well, and I have been very bullish on them," he said. "Valuation is always expensive in India and always has been so."The BSE 150 MidCap Index trades at 24.81 times one-year forward earnings, just below its 10-year average of 26.31 times. The BSE 250 SmallCap Index trades at 22.45 times, above its historical average of 20.65 times."Valuations are broadly around historical averages and earnings growth is expected to be similar across the broader indices," said Nilesh Shah, managing director of Kotak Mahindra AMC. "We think both midcap and smallcap stocks should have a place in investor portfolios."Read more: Largecaps pull ahead of small and mid caps in Q2 profit growth by over 25%. What’s driving the gap?Despite the strong earnings growth, profitability margins weakened in both segments. Among small caps, operating profit margin narrowed to 13.22% from 13.65% in the previous quarter, while net profit margin declined to 6.96% from 7.2%.Midcaps also faced margin pressure, with operating profit margin falling to 17.73% from 18.87% and net profit margin slipping to 9.76% from 10.3% in the previous quarter.

An exciting trend and one we expect to continue.”The Claude developer is expected to price its IPO after Wednesday’s market close, with its shares scheduled to debut on the Nasdaq on Thursday.For live updates on US Markets, click here“We expect significant interest in Anthropic options once they list,” said Garrett DeSimone, head quant at OptionMetrics. “The combination of AI-driven enthusiasm and the lottery-like payoff profile typical of IPOs is likely to draw investors immediately. As one of the most concentrated pure-play exposures to AI, the stock is also likely to be highly volatile.”Ophir Gottlieb, chief executive of Capital Market Laboratories, said that demand for Anthropic options could exceed the interest seen in SpaceX contracts earlier this year. He cited the offering’s oversubscription, its rising valuation and sharp divisions among investors over the outlook for AI stocks.“The AI trade is melting down,” Gottlieb added. “Many feel it is overdone, while many others feel it’s the popping of a bubble. Whenever there are such opposing views in a heated market, we get a lot of option positioning.”Also Read: Anthropic prices IPO at $83 a share, above target range, according to sourcesOptions give investors the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell shares at a predetermined price within a specified period. They can provide a less expensive way to gain exposure to a stock and express views on short-term price swings or longer-term performance.Anthropic’s $64 billion IPO has attracted stronger early institutional demand than SpaceX’s offering, with the order book six times oversubscribed last week, Reuters previously reported.Wall Street firms are preparing for what could be a record market debut by introducing products linked to Anthropic shares, hosting client events and distributing promotional merchandise.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. Anthropic IPO: AI company's listing on Nasdaq to turn thousands of staff into millionaires
items.summary: Anthropic’s upcoming IPO is expected to generate thousands of paper millionaires among current and former employees, potentially creating one of Silicon Valley’s biggest employee wealth windfalls.The Claude maker’s IPO is expected to open on Nasdaq on Thursday at $70-$78 per share, valuing the company at up to $1.4 trillion. Final pricing is expected on Wednesday night.Estimates of employee wealth vary. Hill, a San Francisco-based private-share marketplace, estimates that 598 non-founder employees could hold at least $100 million in equity each after the listing. Private-markets research firm Sacra estimates that around 2,800 current and former employees could have at least $1 million in pretax vested equity at a $1.35 trillion valuation.For live updates on US Markets, click hereBoth estimates are model-based and rely on publicly available information. Reuters could not independently verify them.Anthropic disclosed that employees holding stock options had accumulated $119 billion in paper gains as of September 30, based on a weighted average exercise price of $2.91 per share. Around $73 billion of these gains had vested and could be exercised immediately."The idea of equity appreciating to an amount that is life-changing is something that people strive for," Hill CEO Andrew Benson said. "It doesn't get better than this."Early employees stand to gain the most from Anthropic listingEmployees who joined Anthropic in its early years, including those in junior and administrative roles, could see substantial financial gains because their stock options carried significantly lower exercise prices.Options granted through 2023 and still outstanding at the end of that year had an average exercise price of just 52 cents per share."Early employees who started in a very junior role should have actually a better financial outcome than somebody who joined in a very senior role right before the IPO," Benson said, referring to Anthropic.Non-founder employees will be allowed to sell up to 10% of their holdings on the first trading day, followed by another 35% after the company's fiscal 2026 earnings.Also Read: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller presses for half-point December rate hike as inflation persistsStock awards extended beyond AI talentFounded in 2021, Anthropic expanded its workforce to approximately 5,300 employees by September 30, from around 940 at the end of 2024. Stock-based compensation played a significant role in attracting talent.A May 2024 job advertisement for an administrative business partner offered an annual salary of $140,000-$190,000, while describing equity as "a major component of the total compensation". This highlights how stock awards extended beyond researchers and engineers to administrative and support staff.In 2024, Anthropic granted employees stock options at an average exercise price of $1.30 per share."And as we know from several anecdotes after the SpaceX IPO, this is often enough to help people down the organization chart do quite well in IPO," said Marcelo Ballve, head of research at Sacra.The filing also disclosed that CFO Krishna Rao received 14 million stock options in 2024 at an exercise price of $1.30 each. At the proposed IPO price range, these options could carry approximately $1 billion in gross intrinsic value, before exercise costs and taxes.Ballve noted that equity awards for administrative and entry-level employees are common at venture-backed companies, although some firms reduce upfront grants as they scale. Following its IPO, Anthropic is likely to reserve such grants primarily for recruiting top talent, he added.

Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller presses for half-point December rate hike as inflation persists
items.summary: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller called for a more forceful response to persistent inflation, suggesting policymakers should consider raising interest rates by half a percentage point at their December meeting, according to reports.“We have to be a little more aggressive in our rate hikes to try to get inflation down,” Waller said Wednesday in an interview with CNBC.Inflation data from the past three months imply an annualised rate of about 3.5%, Waller said, significantly above the Fed’s 2% target.For live updates on US Markets, click hereThe central bank could either raise rates by 50 basis points in December or deliver two quarter-point increases in December and January. However, Waller said the second approach would work only if officials clearly signalled that another hike would follow in January.Without a “credible signal” of further tightening, financial markets would not reflect the full impact of the planned increases, he said.“So in that world, if you’re not going to signal this very clearly to markets,” Waller added, “then you have to go 50 in December to put it in place and get it done.”The Fed left its benchmark rate unchanged last month after increasing it in September for the first time in three years. Minutes from the October meeting are scheduled for release at 2 p.m. Wednesday in Washington.Fed officials have broadly agreed that further tightening will be necessary, but they remain divided over how quickly rates should rise.Also Read: Fed policymakers focused on inflation risks in October, with some seeing need for bigger rate hikeWaller first raised the possibility of a half-point increase on November 10, warning that a larger move might be needed to preserve the central bank’s inflation-fighting credibility.His comments came shortly before data showed consumer prices increased more than expected. Core inflation rose 0.3% from the previous month, reaching the level Waller had identified as strengthening the case for a larger rate increase.Waller’s position is more hawkish than that of several other policymakers. New York Fed President John Williams pushed back against an outsized move on Tuesday, although he acknowledged that the central bank still had work to do to return inflation to its 2% target.“I don’t think the situation calls for dramatic action,” Williams said at an Axios event in New York. He added that the Fed’s approach of taking time to evaluate incoming data had worked well.Interest-rate futures indicate that investors expect quarter-point increases in December and January, followed by another hike by April.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

items.summary: Coal India’s wholly owned subsidiary, Mahanadi Coalfields, has raised ₹2,295.24 crore from anchor investors ahead of its Rs 8,981.2-crore initial public offering (IPO), with global financial institutions such as Goldman Sachs, Citigroup and Morgan Stanley featuring in the allocation alongside domestic institutional investors, including Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC).According to the company's stock exchange filing dated November 18, Mahanadi Coalfields has finalised the allocation of 16,87,68,255 equity shares to anchor investors at Rs 136 per share.LIC was the largest individual anchor investor, receiving 4,17,64,690 equity shares worth Rs 567.99 crore.Domestic mutual funds accounted for the largest share of the anchor allocation, receiving 8,95,22,070 equity shares, representing 53.04% of the total allocation. A total of 11 domestic mutual funds participated through 29 schemes.The participating fund houses included Nippon India, WhiteOak Capital, Tata Mutual Fund, HDFC Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential, Aditya Birla Sun Life, Motilal Oswal, Edelweiss, Axis and Baroda BNP Paribas. Invesco India also participated through its Contra Fund.The anchor book also featured several prominent international financial institutions and investment vehicles.Goldman Sachs Bank Europe SE was allocated 7,35,240 shares worth approximately Rs 10 crore, while Citigroup Global Markets Mauritius Private Limited received 3,67,648 shares worth approximately Rs 5 crore.Morgan Stanley Asia Singapore Pte was allocated 36,76,420 shares worth approximately Rs 50 crore. French banking group Société Générale also featured in the list, receiving 40,44,068 shares worth approximately Rs 55 crore.Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA), through its Monsoon investment vehicle, received 17,64,730 shares worth approximately Rs 24 crore.Other overseas-linked investment vehicles named in the filing included Ashoka India Equity Investment Trust, Ashoka WhiteOak ICAV, Integrated Core Strategies Asia Pte Ltd, Venus Investments VCC and Abundantia Capital VCC.Meanwhile, five life insurance companies and pension funds were allocated 4,45,03,615 equity shares, accounting for 26.37% of the total anchor investor allocation.Apart from LIC, the participating insurance companies and pension funds included Bajaj Life Insurance, Edelweiss Life Insurance, Canara HSBC Life Insurance and NPS Trust through UTI Pension Fund's Atal Pension Yojana scheme.Mahanadi Coalfields IPO detailsMahanadi Coalfields IPO is set to open for subscription on November 19, 2026, and will remain open until November 23, giving investors a three-day bidding window.The book-built issue comprises 66.18 crore equity shares and is entirely an offer for sale (OFS) by the existing shareholder, Coal India Limited. Consequently, Mahanadi Coalfields will not receive any proceeds from the public issue, with the entire proceeds, after applicable offer-related expenses and taxes, going to the selling shareholder.The company has fixed the IPO price band at Rs 129-136 per equity share, with a face value of Rs 2 per share. The floor price represents 64.50 times the face value, while the upper end of the price band is 68 times the face value.Investors can bid for a minimum of 110 equity shares and in multiples of 110 shares thereafter. At the upper end of the price band, retail investors will need to invest Rs 14,960 to apply for one lot, subject to applicable investor-category allocation rules.The basis of allotment is expected to be finalised on November 25, while the company's shares are tentatively scheduled to list on the BSE and NSE on November 27, 2026.SBI Capital Markets Limited, Axis Capital Limited, BOB Capital Markets Limited, IDBI Capital Markets & Securities Limited and IIFL Capital Services Limited are the book-running lead managers to the issue. KFin Technologies Limited is the registrar.The grey market premium (GMP) for Mahanadi Coalfields IPO is indicated at around Rs 3 per share, or nearly 2.2% over the upper price band of Rs 136. At this premium, the implied listing price works out to approximately Rs 139 per share. However, the grey market premium is an unofficial indicator of investor sentiment and does not guarantee the listing price or actual returns.About Mahanadi CoalfieldsIncorporated in April 1992, Mahanadi Coalfields Limited (MCL) is a wholly owned subsidiary of Coal India Limited and is India's largest coal producer.The company primarily operates in the mining and production of non-coking coal across Odisha's Talcher and Ib Valley coalfields. Its customer base includes power generation companies and industries such as cement, steel, aluminium, sponge iron and paper.Disclosure: This article has been written by Kumar Gaurav, who is not a Sebi-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. items.title: Gold plunges 3% to one-year low as hawkish Fed lifts dollar, yields
items.summary: Gold plunged to its lowest level in more than a year on Wednesday as hawkish Federal Reserve signals strengthened expectations of further interest-rate increases, lifting the dollar and Treasury yields, Bloomberg News reported.Spot gold fell 3% to $3,736.06 an ounce at 11:43 a.m. ET after touching $3,734.76 earlier in the session, its lowest level since September 26, 2025. US gold futures for December delivery dropped 3.2% to $3,739 an ounce.The metal fell below $3,800 for the first time since September 2025 and was heading for a third consecutive session of losses.“We believe the selloff reflects mounting pressure from a strengthening US dollar, rising Treasury yields and expectations of further monetary tightening. Yesterday’s economic figures reinforced this sentiment,” Naeem Aslam, chief investment officer at Zaye Capital Markets, told Reuters.The dollar rose to a fresh 19-month high as hawkish remarks from Fed officials and recent economic data reinforced expectations of an interest-rate increase next month.For live updates on US Markets, click hereFed Governor Christopher Waller said Wednesday that the central bank needed to respond more aggressively to inflation by either raising rates by half a percentage point in December or signalling a faster pace of increases in 2027.New York Fed President John Williams said Tuesday that the central bank still had work to do to return inflation to its 2% target. St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said the economy would probably require “several interest-rate increases” before spring.Markets see a 92% probability of a 25-basis-point increase in December and an 8% chance of a larger 50-basis-point move, according to the CME FedWatch tool. They are also pricing in quarter-point increases in January and by April.Expectations of tighter policy have pushed the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield toward its longest stretch above 5% in nearly two decades. Higher yields increase the opportunity cost of holding non-interest-bearing assets such as gold.The stronger dollar also makes bullion more expensive for buyers using other currencies.“It is a tough environment for gold, particularly with buying interest still subdued,” said Christopher Wong, a strategist at Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp, to Bloomberg. He said the market would remain cautious without a clear catalyst for a reversal.Gold has lost more than a quarter of its value since the US-Iran war began in late February. The conflict has pushed energy prices higher, fueled inflation and prompted central banks to tighten monetary policy.Investors are now awaiting minutes from the Fed’s October 27-28 meeting for further clues about the rate path. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh avoided directly addressing monetary policy earlier this week, consistent with his stated preference not to provide near-term rate guidance.“If the minutes reinforce concerns about persistent inflation and support additional tightening, Treasury yields and the dollar could strengthen further, potentially extending gold’s decline below $3,800,” Aslam added.Other precious metals also fell sharply. Spot silver declined 5.3% to $44.88 an ounce after touching its lowest level since September 26, 2025.Platinum dropped 4.6% to $1,363.50 after hitting its lowest level since September 17, 2025, extending its year-to-date loss to 33%. Palladium fell 2.6% to $945.95, its lowest level since early November.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

items.summary:
India's gold imports in the current fiscal could decline to USD 40 billion, down from about USD 72 billion in FY26, as the duty hike has helped slow inbound shipments, a top official said on Wednesday.
Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said the duty hike effected from May has "slowed down" gold imports "a bit" so far this year, from around USD 60 billion every year. This has also helped manage the trade deficit, he said.
In May, the government had hiked import duty on gold and silver to 15 per cent, from 6 per cent, to contain non-essential imports.
India imported USD 71.98 billion gold in FY26, up from USD 58.01 billion in FY25.
Gold imports declined about 40 per cent to USD 24.78 billion during April-October this year, from about USD 41.24 billion in the corresponding period in 2025.
"I think... this year we will end up with USD 35-40 billion of gold imports. I think that is manageable in the current year... The current duty structure has a positive impact on the gold import," .

items.title: Iranian army claims it targeted US' Ali Al Salem air base in Kuwait
items.summary:
The Iranian army claimed early Wednesday it targeted US Ali Al Salem air base in Kuwait with drones, triggering the air defence alerts in the oil-rich Gulf country for the first time in weeks.
The army claimed it had targeted air defence systems, as well as drone and missile launch platforms, according to a statement carried by Iran's state broadcaster.
US Central Command, which oversees US forces in the Middle East, did not immediately comment.
Earlier Wednesday, Kuwait's Army said its air defences were intercepting drone attacks but did not immediately report any damage. The country's Foreign Ministry condemned the repeated Iranian "criminal" attacks, and said they threatened Kuwait's security and stability.
Iran also recently claimed attacks against US military targets in the tiny island kingdom of Bahrain. Iran targeted US facilities and interests in the neighbouring Gulf countries following the US and Israeli strikes against it on Feb 28.

items.summary: Shares of PVR Inox jumped around 4% on Wednesday, extending gains to over 6% in two days after ratings agency CRISIL revised its outlook for the firm’s long-term bank facilities and non-convertible debentures (NCDs) to ‘Positive’ from ‘Stable’.PVR Inox shares hit a fresh 52-week high of around Rs 1,740 apiece on NSE today, pushing its market capitalisation above Rs 17,060 crore. Along with the outlook upgrade, CRISIL Ratings also reaffirmed its 'Crisil AA' rating on the long term debt instruments of the company.Why did Crisil upgrade its outlook for PVR Inox?The rating on the short-term bank facilities and commercial paper programme has been reaffirmed at 'Crisil A1+'. The ratings agency said the outlook upgrade was driven by expectations of sustained growth in the company’s scale of operations across multiple revenue streams and improvement in operating margin strengthening its business risk profile. The outlook revision also accounts for the strengthening of the company’s financial risk profile by becoming a net cash company during the first half of fiscal 2027.Also read | District's PVR INOX ticket sales jump 60%, rivals lag at 4%The structural improvement is driven by PVR Inox’s ability to monetise its network more consistently across content cycles, thereby reducing content concentration risk, Crisil said. It added that the content ecosystem has become increasingly diversified, with admissions being supported by a broader mix of Hindi, regional and Hollywood content. The industry has also witnessed increasing success of mid-budget films which lowers the dependence on a few marquee releases and provides greater stability to admissions and occupancy.Alternate content initiatives such as re-releases, concert screenings, anime content and sports broadcasts have also emerged as supplementary demand drivers and improve utilisation of the existing screen network, Crisil said. It noted that the concerns around OTT-led disruption have also moderated as the theatrical-first release model has been re-established, with producers increasingly using theatrical performance as the primary benchmark for content monetisation on OTT, highlighting the complementary nature of theatrical and digital channels.PVR Inox’s business risk profile is also supported by increasing geographical diversification as the company continues to expand its presence in southern India and tier 2 and 3 markets, which benefit from strong movie-going culture, multiple thriving film industries and relatively low multiplex penetration, the ratings agency said, further noting that the company’s screen portfolio in southern markets increased from 31% at the end of fiscal 2023 to 34% in at the end of first half of fiscal 2027, with more than 35% of screen additions over the past three years originating from the region. “This diversification supports admissions visibility and reduces dependence on any single language or regional content cycle,” it said.Crisil further highlighted PVR Inox’s earnings, pointing out that the company demonstrated healthy revenue growth driven by a mix of increasing admissions, increasing average ticket prices (ATP), higher spends per head (SPH), and improving monetisation of its customer base. Net debt reduced, aided by strong accrual generation and proceeds from the divestment of the 4700 BC business for about Rs 227 crore in January 2026. Despite completion of a Rs 300 crore maiden share buyback in the first half of fiscal 2027, leverage metrics are expected to remain comfortable, the ratings agency said. It expects the company’s net worth to remain healthy and gradually improve over the medium term, supported by strong accrual.“The ratings reflect the company’s strong market position with an established brand, expectation of further improvement in operating efficiency, led by synergistic benefits and premiumisation, and a strong financial risk profile. These strengths are partially offset by inherent volatility of the film exhibition business with operating performance remaining dependent on the quality and timing of content releases and evolving consumer preferences,” it said.Also read | PVR INOX bets on smaller multiplexes as single-screens declinePVR Inox share pricePVR Inox shares jumped more than 9% in a week and 23% in a month. This comes amid blockbuster releases including Ranbir Kapoor-starrer Ramayana: Part 1. The stock has so far gained more than 70% in 2026.The shares of the multiplex chain operator have delivered 55% returns over one year. In the longer term, the stock gained more than 4.5% in three years and 2% in five years. items.title: Cambridge Dictionary chooses 'human' as word of the year amid AI fears
items.summary:
Fears of artificial intelligence inspired the Cambridge Dictionary to flip back to the 15th century for the word that best captures the 2026 cultural zeitgeist.
"Human," the dictionary's word of the year, is not just a throwback but also a backlash of sorts that reflects the debate over how AI has blurred the lines between machines and people.
"AI is changing how we talk about being human," said Colin McIntosh, the dictionary's lexicographer. "Fears about what humans may lose when we outsource our thinking have made us reconsider the extent to which we rely on AI: from top mathematicians to teachers of young children."
The adjective derived from the Latin "humanus" and in use since the 1450s is defined by Cambridge as "having the qualities, faults and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals or machines."

items.title: ACME Solar shares rally 3% as subsidiary signs 150 MW hybrid power project PPA with NTPC
items.summary: Shares of ACME Solar rallied up to 3% on Thursday, hitting an intraday high of Rs 416 on the NSE. The gains came after the company, through its subsidiary ACME Alpha Renewable, signed a Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) with NTPC for a 150 MW Inter-State Transmission System (ISTS)-connected hybrid power project at a tariff of Rs 3.21 per unit under NTPC’s Hybrid-IV tranche. According to a filing with the exchange, the company said that the tariff for this project has already been adopted by the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC). The order has been awarded by NTPC, with the scheduled commencement of power supply set for June 30, 2028. The project will have a tenure of 25 years from the scheduled commencement date.Also Read | Nvidia shares jump 5% in after hours as quarterly earnings beat estimates. Is the storm around Huang’s exit finally over?The hybrid project, spanning Bhadla in Rajasthan, Jambkhabalia in Gujarat and Mandsaur in Madhya Pradesh, will combine solar and wind energy with suitable energy storage solutions.It is designed to provide reliable and dispatchable power throughout the day while meeting offtakers' requirements during peak demand hours. CTU transmission connectivity has been secured for the Jambkhabalia and Mandsaur locations.The project marks an important step towards ACME Solar's goal of contributing to India's clean energy transition. Following the signing of this PPA, the company's under-construction, PPA-backed portfolio stands at 5,080 MW, out of a total under-construction contracted capacity of 5,380 MW.“This PPA with NTPC reinforces our focus on delivering reliable renewable power aligned with the evolving needs of India’s energy market. By combining solar, wind and energy storage, the project will help meet peak-hour demand and support India’s clean energy transition,” said Nikhil Dhingra, Joint MD and CEO of ACME Solar.The company also clarified that neither its promoters, promoter group nor group companies have any interest in the entity that awarded the contract. It added that the order does not fall under related-party transactions.On November 16, the company announced that its wholly owned subsidiary, ACME Greentech Sixteen, had signed a Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) with Rewa Ultra Mega Solar to set up a 220 MW solar project with a Battery Energy Storage System at Morena Solar Park in Madhya Pradesh.The project has a scheduled commercial operation date of December 31, 2027, and a tariff of Rs 2.764 per unit.Also Read | IIFL Finance shares jump 5% after 13% stake changes hands in block deal, Fairfax likely sellerACME Solar share priceACME Solar shares have gained around 0.68% over the past month and 73.56% so far this calendar year. US spy agency's internal network faces outage during 'routine maintenance'
items.summary:
An internal network the National Security Agency uses to communicate classified information was offline Tuesday after what one US official described as "routine maintenance."
A defence official said that the problem affected NSANet, a classified internal network used by employees of the agency. A different US official said that the NSA "experienced temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance."
The official added, "while some internal systems were affected, mission/critical capabilities remain fully operational and our ability to defend national security continues."
Another person familiar with the matter said the issue occurred during routine patching. The three individuals spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss non-public information.
The NSA episode is the latest in a series of cyber-related disruptions to critical government and private sector functions in the last week, including one Friday that resulted in a ground stop of air traffic in the United States ..

FAA halts installation of Juniper routers after air traffic disruption
items.summary:
The Federal Aviation Administration has paused the installation of the routers that were linked to last week's national ground stop, and turned off any Juniper routers that were already installed.
The decision was made after technicians linked Friday's disruption of key air traffic control systems to one of these routers that had just been installed in El Dorado, Arkansas.
For now, the FAA is relying on older Cisco routers that have been in place for 25 years to continue operating the network while they investigate the cause of Friday's problems at 17 of the nation's 22 regional air traffic control centers.
The routers that malfunctioned last week are being tested in a lab at the headquarters of the company that installed them named L3Harris.

Char Dham Yatra sees 29% rise in pilgrims, 63% jump in fatalities in 2026
items.summary:
More than 65.65 lakh pilgrims visited the Char Dham shrines and Hemkund Sahib in 2026, a 29 per cent increase over the previous year, even as pilgrim fatalities rose by 63 per cent, according to a Dehradun-based non-profit organisation.
A total of 65,65,197 pilgrims visited the five shrines this year, compared to 51,07,346 in 2025, an increase of 14,57,851, the analysis by social and environmental non-profit SDC Foundation showed.
Among the shrines, Badrinath recorded the highest footfall at 23,49,345, followed by Kedarnath (19,33,138), Gangotri (10,07,177), Yamunotri (8,84,841) and Hemkund Sahib (3,90,696).
The NGO's analysis of the state government's daily bulletins found that pilgrim numbers increased across all five shrines, but at varying rates. Praveen Upreti of SDC Foundation, along with its founder Anoop Nautiyal, collated the data.
Badrinath and Hemkund Sahib reported the highest growth at 42 per cent each, followed by Yamunotri (37 per cent) and Gangotri (33 per cent). ..

India said the targeting of commercial shipping and civilian infrastructure must end.
"Of the 24 Indian nationals on board, 21 have been safely evacuated ashore at Khasab, two injured Indian crew members have been admitted to hospital, while one Indian national remains missing," it added.

items.summary: Mumbai | New Delhi: Bain Capital-backed RSB Group plans an initial public offering (IPO) of up to ₹4,000 crore, people aware of the matter told ET. The auto-parts maker has raised about ₹500 crore in a pre-IPO round from a clutch of new investors."The company is contemplating filing the draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) next month (December) and the issue size is likely to be around ₹4,000 crore," a person aware of the developments told ET.The company has appointed Axis Capital, Jefferies and HSBC Securities and Capital Matkets as book-running lead managers for the proposed issue.Read more: Dalal Street’s top investors defy market slump; Mukul Agrawal tops Q2 wealth gainsIn the run-up to the proposed issue, five new investors collectively bought less than 10% in the company. These investors include White Oak Capital, promoted by former Goldman Sachs executive Prashant Khemka, JM Financial, 360One Asset, Abakkus Four2Eigth opportunities fund and Novaa One. The Behera family, promoters of RSB Group, also participated in the round, providing additional capital to the company.RSB Group did not give financial details of the transactions.Emails sent to the company and bankers remained unanswered until the publication of this report.RSB Group makes transmission equipment for medium and heavy commercial vehicle makers such as Tata and Ashok Leyland. The Pune-headquartered company has plants in multiple locations in India and Mexico.Bain Capital struck a partnership with RSB Group in 2024 but has not disclosed the size of the stake it owns in the company.The company operates 19 manufacturing plants in India and two in Mexico, serving Tier-I customers across India and the US.RSB manufactures precision-engineered drivetrain components for commercial vehicles, passenger cars, construction equipment and agricultural machinery. items.title: US judge blocks Trump curbs on student work
items.summary: A federal judge on Tuesday blocked President Donald Trump's administration from restricting the types of internships and other practical training opportunities available to international students attending US universities on visas.US District Judge Julia Kobick in Boston issued an injunction barring the US Department of Homeland Security from enforcing two August directives that higher education groups said had abruptly disrupted training opportunities for foreign students nationwide.Kobick, an appointee of former Democratic President Joe Biden, ruled in a lawsuit filed last month by four organizations, including the Association of American Universities and the Presidents' Alliance on Higher Education and Immigration.It marked the latest victory for plaintiffs challenging efforts by the Trump administration to impose restrictions on student visa holders as part of its hardline immigration agenda. On Monday, a different federal judge in Boston struck down a new rule that would limit how long ‌foreign students can remain in the US without applying for extensions.DHS declined to comment.The education groups in the case before Kobick argued that DHS had sharply narrowed rules that for more than 35 years governed international students' participation in internships and other practical training through a program known as curricular practical training, or CPT.They said foreign students historically could take part in school-authorized internships and training opportunities as long as they were directly related to their field of study and formed an integral part of an established curriculum.According to the plaintiffs, the government long interpreted that standard to allow participation when training either carried academic credit or was required to earn a degree.Amazon and Tesla were the top two employers of CPT students in 2024, when 140,775 student visa holders were authorized to participate in CPT overall, according to US Immigration and Customs Enforcement.But in August, DHS, which oversees ICE, issued messages telling universities that internships and other opportunities qualified only if they were mandatory for every student in a degree program and did not cover elective training taken for academic credit.The agency said it had seen an increase in CPT authorizations it believed did not comply with program requirements and would increase scrutiny of approvals.Kobick found the directives were likely arbitrary and capricious under the Administrative Procedure Act as DHS had failed to acknowledge that it was making a "fundamental" change to the government's longstanding interpretation of the program's rules."Correct or not, this new interpretation is inconsistent with the government's previous position," she wrote.
